sentences: On a planet, the councillor, a member of the planet's high council, sentences three criminals, one of them a general, to the prison zone.
He warns the council that the planet will be destroyed by its exploding red supergiant sun, but they dismiss his concerns.
Before the planet's destruction, the councillor and his wife send their infant son to another planet.
There, the boy's unique physiology grants him evolving superhuman abilities.
The infant's spaceship touches down near a town.
He is found by a couple, who are astonished when the infant lifts their truck.
They adopt him, giving him a name.
As he grows, hiding his powers, his adoptive father believes the boy was sent to this planet for a special purpose.
Years later, after losing his adoptive father to a fatal heart attack, the teenaged boy is summoned by a glowing green crystal from his spaceship which is hidden in the barn.
This leads him to the far north, where a fortress, mirroring his home planet's architecture, ascends from the ice.
Inside, the councillor's hologram reveals the boy's heritage and trains him over the next twelve years.
Emerging in a blue-and-red suit bearing his family's crest, he is cautioned against changing human history.
The hero adopts a new persona as a mild-mannered reporter, and starts wearing glasses to disguise his true appearance.
He is hired by a newspaper in the city, where he meets an investigative journalist.

The hero debuts his new costume by saving the journalist from a helicopter accident and, over the rest of the evening, uses his powers in public acts of heroism, gaining immediate fame as the "caped wonder".
Thanks to the hero's disguise, he successfully keeps his true identity secret from the journalist and his colleagues.

The newspaper's chief seeks more information on this new hero; the hero arranges for the journalist to interview his new alter-ego and, afterwards, takes her on a flight over the city, leading her to coin his name.
A criminal mastermind discovers a joint army/navy missile test and plots to target a fault line with reprogrammed missiles, though one is misdirected by his bumbling assistant.
Suspecting the hero's interference, the villain identifies a meteorite from the hero's home planet, lethal to the hero.
With his assistant and his girlfriend, the villain retrieves it and traps the hero in his lair, revealing his plan to sink the western part of the country, making his desert land prime coastline.
He weakens the hero using the meteorite, now given a name, and informs him of the misdirected missile set for a town.
Concerned for her mother in that town, the girlfriend frees the hero, urging him to first stop the eastbound missile.
He sends it to space but misses the westbound missile, which triggers severe earthquakes in the west, endangering landmarks like a bridge and a dam.
The hero counteracts the devastation by mending the fault line.
As the hero rescues others, the journalist is trapped in her car by an aftershock, suffocating before he can save her.
Distraught and enraged over his failure to save the journalist, he disregards the councillor's warning against altering history.
Heeding his adoptive father's belief in his purpose, the hero accelerates around the planet, traveling back in time to prevent the journalist's death and the missile's detonation.
After saving the coast, he imprisons the villain and his assistant, then soars into the sunrise.
On a high school field trip, the young man visits a university genetics laboratory with his best friend and his crush.
There, he is bitten by a genetically engineered spider, and falls ill upon returning home.
Meanwhile, the friend's father tests a performance-enhancing chemical on himself in an attempt to secure a military contract for the company he founded.
The chemical gives him superhuman strength but causes him to go insane and kill one of his scientists.
The next day, the young man develops spider-like abilities, including enhanced strength, senses, agility, and speed; organic webbing in his wrists; and the ability to cling to walls.
He also is no longer near-sighted, and now has clear vision without requiring glasses.
Hoping to buy a car to impress the girl, the young man enters an underground wrestling event and wins his match, but is swindled out of his earnings.
When the wrestling organizer is robbed, a bitter young man steps out of the way, allowing the thief to escape.
Soon after, the young man's uncle is killed by the same thief.
The young man pursues the thief, who eventually falls to his death.
Meanwhile, the friend's father, now crazed, sabotages a product test by a rival of the company and kills several people.
Upon graduating, the young man begins using his abilities to fight crime, donning a costume and adopting an alias.
The publisher of a newspaper hires the young man as a freelance photographer, since he can provide high-quality images of the hero.
When the company's board of directors decides to oust the friend's father and sell the company, the friend's father uses a disguise to assassinate them during a festival.
As the hero, the young man fends off the friend's father and rescues the girl.
Afterwards, the publisher bestows a name upon the mysterious masked killer.
The friend's father offers the young man a place at his side, but the young man refuses.
They fight, and the young man flees after being wounded.
The young man's aunt invites the girl, the friend, and the friend's father for Thanksgiving dinner.
The friend's father notices the young man's injury and deduces that he is the hero.
Later, the friend's father attacks and injures the aunt, who is hospitalized.
The young man is still unaware of the villain's identity, but realizes that the villain is targeting his loved ones.
While visiting the hospital, the girl confesses to the young man her infatuation with the hero, who has rescued her twice.
The friend, who is dating the girl, sees her holding the young man's hand and assumes she has feelings for him.
A distraught friend tells his father about the young man's infatuation with the girl.
That night, the friend's father captures the girl and a tramway car full of children.
He tells the young man to choose whom to rescue, then drops them both from a bridge.
The young man saves everyone, then lowers them onto a nearby barge for safety.
The friend's father, enraged, throws the young man into a nearby abandoned building, then brutally beats him.
After the friend's father reveals his intentions to kill the girl, the young man finds the strength to fight back.
The friend's father reveals his identity and begs forgiveness, discreetly preparing to impale the young man with his glider.
Warned by his spider-sense, the young man dodges the attack, and the glider fatally skewers the friend's father instead.
Before dying, the friend's father begs the young man not to reveal his identity to the friend.
The young man takes the friend's father's body to the family house, where the friend confronts him, but the young man escapes.
At the friend's father's funeral, the friend vows revenge on the hero, who he mistakenly believes killed his father.
The girl then confesses to the young man that she loves him.
However, the young man feels he must protect her from his enemies, so he hides his true feelings and tells her they can only be friends.
As the young man leaves, he recalls his uncle's words: "With great power comes great responsibility."
In 1982, a young boy is accidentally blinded by radioactive waste.
This is shortly after he witnesses his father, a washed-up boxer, extorting money for a local mob boss.
Despite this, the boy's remaining senses are dramatically enhanced, giving him superhuman agility and sonar-like hearing.
Feeling responsible for his son's accident, the father is inspired to abandon his life of crime and recommit to his boxing career.
This leads to a dramatic comeback.

Later, after the mob boss reveals that he enabled the father's comeback by bribing his previous opponents to let him win, he attempts to bribe the father to throw his next match, then has him murdered once he refuses. 20 years later, the boy, now grown, works as an attorney in the city with his friend, providing legal representation pro bono to clients whom he believes are actually innocent.
By night, he fights crime as a costumed vigilante.

A newspaper reporter who chronicles the vigilante's exploits attracts attention for a series of articles on a crime lord, a shadowy underworld figure who allegedly controls all of the city's organized crime.
Unbeknownst to the reporter, the crime lord is actually a brutal mobster who poses as a legitimate businessman.
The lawyer falls in love with a Greek-American woman skilled in martial arts, unaware that she is the daughter of the crime lord's lieutenant.
Later, when the lieutenant attempts to end his relationship with the crime lord, the crime lord hires a hitman with preternatural aim to kill him.
The hitman steals the vigilante's weaponized baton and impales the lieutenant with it, killing him and framing the vigilante.
Afterward, the reporter deduces that the lawyer is the vigilante after realizing that he disguises his baton as a white cane.
Meanwhile, the hitman is next assigned by the crime lord to kill the woman.
Believing the vigilante to be responsible for her father's murder, she attempts to take revenge by killing him.
The woman tracks him down and challenges him to a fight before incapacitating him by stabbing him through the shoulder.
The vigilante protests that he did not kill her father, but she does not listen until she forcibly unmasks him and discovers that he is the lawyer.
Moments later, when the hitman finds the woman, the lawyer is helpless as the assassin seemingly kills her.
Wounded, the lawyer takes refuge in a church, but the hitman ambushes him by exploiting his weakness to loud sound.
When the police swarm the church, the hitman reveals that the crime lord killed the lawyer's father, leaving behind a rose on his body as a calling card.
Soon, the lawyer gains the upper hand and throws him from the bell tower after a police sniper shoots him through both hands, depriving him of his powerful aim.
Determined to avenge the woman and his father, the lawyer ambushes the crime lord in his office.
In the ensuing fight, he ultimately triumphs against the crime lord's brute strength by using his sonar hearing to see him after he is drenched in water from a sprinkler head.
During their confrontation, the crime lord admits that he killed the lawyer's father on the mob boss's orders and that the woman's death was nothing but a casualty.
As the police arrive to arrest the crime lord, he threatens to reveal the vigilante's identity to the world, but the lawyer points out that no one will ever believe that the vigilante is a blind man.
Some time after the woman's death, the lawyer visits the roof of his apartment, where the two of them first kissed.
There he unexpectedly finds the woman's necklace with her name engraved upon it in braille, hinting that she might still be alive.
The reporter prepares to publish an article revealing the vigilante's identity, but decides against it at the last minute, finally accepting that the vigilante's efforts have improved the city.

The reporter exits the newspaper office into the night outside and sees the lawyer on a roof, saying "Go get 'em", to which the vigilante nods his head and takes off, leaping off the building to pursue his nightly crimefighting routine.
Elsewhere, a heavily bandaged hitman awakens in a heavily guarded hospital room and kills a fly with a syringe needle.
The industrialist, who has inherited a defense contractor from his late father, tours in a war-torn country with his best friend and military liaison to demonstrate a new missile.
After the demonstration, his convoy is ambushed by a terrorist group, and the industrialist is gravely wounded by a missile used by the attackers—one of his company's own.
He is captured and imprisoned in a cave by the terrorists.
A fellow captive and doctor implants an electromagnet into the industrialist's chest to keep the shrapnel shards that wounded him from reaching his heart and killing him.
The terrorists' leader offers the industrialist freedom in exchange for building one of the new missiles for the group, but he and the doctor believe that the leader will not keep his word.

The industrialist and the doctor secretly build a small, powerful electric generator called an arc reactor to power the industrialist's electromagnet and construct a prototype armored suit to aid in their escape.
Although they keep the suit hidden, the terrorists discover their intentions and attack the workshop.
The doctor sacrifices himself to divert them while the suit powers up.
The armored industrialist battles his way out of the cave to find the dying doctor, then burns the terrorists' weapons and flies away, crashing in the desert and destroying the suit.
After being rescued by his friend, the industrialist returns home and announces that his company will cease manufacturing weapons.
His father's old partner and the company's manager advises the industrialist that this will bankrupt the company and ruin his father's legacy.
In his home workshop, the industrialist builds a sleeker, more powerful version of his improvised armor suit as well as a more powerful arc reactor for it and his chest after testing a prototype.
His personal assistant places the original reactor inside a small glass showcase.
Though the manager requests details, a suspicious industrialist decides to keep his work to himself.
At a charity event, a reporter informs the industrialist that his company's weapons were recently delivered to the terrorists and are being used to attack the doctor's home village.
The industrialist dons his new armor and flies to the war-torn country, where he fends off the terrorists and saves the villagers.
While flying home, the industrialist is intercepted by the air force and reveals his secret identity to his friend over the phone to end the attack.

Meanwhile, the terrorists gather the pieces of the industrialist's prototype suit and meet with the manager, who has been trafficking arms to the terrorists and has staged a coup to replace the industrialist as the company's CEO by hiring the terrorists to kill him.
He subdues the leader, has his group killed, and reverse-engineers a massive new armor suit from the wreckage.
Seeking to track his company's illegal shipments, the industrialist sends the assistant to hack into its database.
She discovers that the manager hired the terrorists to kill the industrialist, but the group altered their plans when they realized they had a direct route to the industrialist's weapons.
The assistant meets with an agent of an intelligence agency to inform him of the manager's activities.

The manager's scientists are unable to replicate the industrialist's miniaturized arc reactor, so the manager enters the industrialist's home, stuns the industrialist, and steals the one from his chest.
The industrialist manages to replace it with his original reactor.
The assistant and several of the agency's agents attempt to arrest the manager, but he dons his suit and overpowers them.
The industrialist fights the manager but is outmatched without his new reactor to run his suit at full capacity.
The fight carries the industrialist and the manager to the top of the company's building, where the industrialist instructs the assistant to overload the large arc reactor powering the building.
This unleashes a massive electrical surge that causes the manager to fall into the reactor, and he is killed in the explosion.
The next day, at a press conference, the industrialist publicly admits to being the superhero the press has named.
In a post-credits scene, the agency's director visits the industrialist at his home, telling him that he has become part of a "bigger universe", and that he wants to discuss an initiative.
When the publisher of a newspaper dies, his estranged son takes over the newspaper and fires most of his father's personal staff.
The son later rehires a mechanic skilled in martial arts and coffee brewing as his assistant and the two become friends.
The son convinces the mechanic they should become crime-fighters.
The mechanic develops a car, outfitted with several gadgets and weapons, which they give a nickname.
The son plans to capture a Russian mobster who intends to unite the crime families of the city under his command.
To get the mobster's attention, the son uses the newspaper to publish articles about his alter ego and mark the alter ego as a villain.
The son and the mechanic blow up several of the mobster's meth labs, leaving calling cards behind.
The district attorney frets over public perception that he cannot stop the alter ego.
The son asks his researcher out, but she invites the mechanic instead, making the son jealous.

The mechanic learns from her that mobsters often offer a peace summit to rivals in order to get close enough to kill them; the son then tells the mechanic that the mobster has offered them such a meeting.
The mechanic tries dissuading him, but the son ignores him.
Once there, the mobster tries to kill them, but the mechanic manages to save them and escape.
Upon returning to the mansion, the son and the mechanic start arguing.
In a fit of rage, the son fires both the mechanic and the researcher.
The son discovers that the district attorney is corrupt and an ally of the mobster.
The district attorney reveals the publisher found out and tried to expose him, so he had the mobster assassinate him.
When the son reveals he recorded the district attorney's confession the mechanic arrives, with the mobster and some of his men outside waiting for the alter ego to kill the son.
After the son apologizes to the mechanic, he accepts and saves him.
The mobster and his men storm the restaurant and attempt to murder the duo who escape in another such car.
The mobster, the district attorney, and their men chase the son and the mechanic throughout the city, ending in a fight at the newspaper office.

During the fight the son and the mechanic kill the mobster, but when they realize they didn't record the district attorney's confession the mechanic uses the heavily damaged car to run the district attorney off the top of the building.
The son and the mechanic hide out at the researcher's house, where she learns their alter egos.

The next morning, the son promotes an employee to chief editor and pretends to get shot by the mechanic posing as his alter ego, solidifying the alter ego as a vigilante and allowing the son to get treated in a hospital for a wound he received the night before.
In 1996, aboard a research vessel, a treasure hunter and his team explore the wreck of a ship, hoping to find a necklace.
Instead, they recover a safe containing a drawing of a young woman wearing the necklace.
The sketch is dated April 14, 1912, the day the ship struck an iceberg and sank, resulting in about 1,500 deaths.
After seeing a television report about the discovery, the centenarian heroine contacts the treasure hunter, revealing she is the woman in the drawing.
Hoping she can help locate the necklace, the treasure hunter brings the heroine and her granddaughter aboard the research vessel, where the heroine recounts her experience on the ship.
In 1912, the 17-year-old heroine boards the ship at port with her wealthy fiancé and her mother.
The heroine is unhappy in the loveless engagement, but her mother stresses that the marriage will resolve their financial problems.
The heroine contemplates suicide by jumping from the ship's stern, but is stopped by a poor nomadic artist.
The artist and the heroine form a friendship, and the artist confesses his feelings for her.
Though initially resistant, the heroine realizes she has fallen in love with the artist, despite the fiancé's and her mother's disapproval.
The heroine brings the artist to her stateroom and asks him to draw her nude, wearing only the necklace.
Afterward, they evade the fiancé's valet and have sex in a car in the cargo hold.
On the forward deck, they witness the ship's collision with an iceberg and overhear officers discussing the severity of the situation.
When the fiancé discovers the artist's sketch of the heroine, he has the valet plant the necklace on the artist, framing him for theft.
The artist is arrested and locked in the master-at-arms' office, and the fiancé pockets the necklace.
As the ship sinks, women and children are prioritized for the lifeboats.
The heroine rescues the artist, and they return to the deck, where the fiancé urges the heroine to board a lifeboat, claiming he and the artist will board another.
The fiancé unwittingly wraps his coat, containing the necklace, around her.
As her lifeboat is lowered, the heroine jumps back onto the ship, unwilling to leave the artist behind.
Enraged, the fiancé grabs a pistol and chases them through the flooding ship, but gives up when they escape.
The fiancé joins a lifeboat by pretending to be a child's father.
As the flooded bow sinks, the stern rises into the air, and the artist and the heroine cling to the railing.
The ship splits in two, and the stern sinks into the freezing water with the remaining passengers.
The artist helps the heroine onto floating debris and makes her promise to survive and live a full life.
The artist dies from hypothermia, but the heroine is saved by a returning lifeboat and rescued by another ship.
The heroine hides from the fiancé and her mother and gives her surname as the artist's on her arrival in the city.
In the present, the heroine reveals that the fiancé committed suicide after losing his fortune in the 1929 stock market crash.
She tells the research vessel's crew that the artist saved her in every possible way, and laments that her memories are all that she has left of him.
Touched by her account, the treasure hunter abandons his search for the necklace.
Alone at night on the stern of the research vessel, the heroine, who has kept the necklace in her possession, drops it into the sea above the wreck.
Later, as she lies in her bed, photographs on her dresser depict a life of freedom and adventure inspired by the artist.
Aboard the pristine ship, the young heroine reunites with the artist at the grand staircase, applauded by the passengers and crew who died in the sinking.
In 1981, a feather lands at a bus stop in a city; the hero collects it, then recounts his life story to strangers on a bus bench.
In a fictional city during the 1950s, the hero is fitted with leg braces to correct a curved spine.
His mother runs a boarding house out of their home.
Among their tenants is a performer, who incorporates the hero's jerky dance movements into his performances.
On his first day of school, the hero befriends a girl.
The hero is often bullied because of his physical disability and low intelligence.
While fleeing from several bullies, his leg braces break off, revealing the hero to be a very fast runner.
In 1963, after inadvertently interrupting a practice session of a university football team, the hero is noticed by the coach, who offers him an athletic scholarship.
The hero plays as a kick returner, is later named to the all-star college football team, and meets the president
at the presidential residence.
He also witnesses the governor's stand in the schoolhouse door, during which the hero returns a dropped book to a student.
After graduating college in 1966, the hero enlists into the army where he befriends a fellow soldier, who convinces the hero to go into the shrimping business with him after their service.
They arrive in the war zone in 1967 and serve with an infantry division in a river delta.
Their platoon is ambushed during a patrol.
Despite being shot, the hero saves several wounded platoon mates – including his lieutenant, who has suffered severe leg injuries – but the fellow soldier is killed.
The hero is awarded a medal for his heroism by the president.
At an anti-war march, the hero meets an activist and briefly reunites with his childhood friend, who has been living a hippie life.

While healing from his injury, the hero develops a talent for ping-pong, and becomes a sports celebrity as he competes against Chinese teams in ping-pong diplomacy, earning him an interview alongside a musician on a talk show, influencing a song.
He spends the 1971 New Year's Eve in the city with the lieutenant, who lost his legs as a result of his injuries and has become a deeply embittered alcoholic.
The hero meets the president, who arranges a room for the hero in a hotel, where he unwittingly exposes a scandal.

Discharged from the army, the hero returns to his home state and endorses a ping-pong paddle manufacturer, using the earnings to buy a shrimping boat in a coastal town, fulfilling his promise to the fellow soldier.
The lieutenant joins the hero in 1974, but their business initially starts off slow.
The pair's fortunes turn after their boat becomes the sole survivor of a hurricane.
They create a shrimp company; the lieutenant reconciles himself to his disabilities, and finally thanks the hero for saving his life.
The hero returns home to his mother as she dies of cancer.
The lieutenant invests their money into what he initially believes is a "fruit company," which later turns out to be a computer company, and the two become millionaires.
The hero shares his earnings with the community and the fellow soldier's family.
His childhood friend returns to stay with the hero in 1976, recovering from years of abuse, drugs, and prostitution.
The hero proposes marriage, but his childhood friend turns him down.
After a night of sexual intercourse, his childhood friend leaves the next morning.
Heartbroken, the hero spends the next three years in a relentless cross-country run.
In 1981, the hero reveals that he is waiting at the bus stop because he received a letter from his childhood friend inviting him to visit.
She introduces him to their son, who is named after him. His childhood friend tells the hero she is sick with an unknown incurable virus, and the three move back to the hero's home.
His childhood friend and the hero marry, but she dies a year later.
The hero sends his son off on his first day of school as the feather from the movie's opening floats away in the wind.
In a world where toys are sentient but pretend to be lifeless around humans, a group of toys, led by a sheriff, are preparing to move to a new house with their young owner and his family.
During the party for the boy's sixth birthday, the toys—including five others—become concerned that the boy might receive a new toy that will replace them.
The boy receives an action figure, who believes that he is an actual space ranger and does not know that he is a toy.
The action figure impresses the others with his electronic features and becomes the boy's new favorite toy, much to the sheriff's jealousy.
Two days before the move, the boy's family plans to have dinner at a pizza restaurant, and the boy is allowed to bring one toy along.
To ensure the boy brings him instead of the action figure, the sheriff tries to trap the action figure behind the boy's desk but accidentally knocks him out the window.
Believing the sheriff pushed the action figure on purpose, the other toys rebel against the sheriff until the boy takes him into the car, with the action figure following.
When the car stops at a gas station, the action figure furiously confronts the sheriff.
The two fight, fall out of the car, and are left behind, but then manage to hitch a ride on a delivery truck from the pizza restaurant.
At the pizza restaurant, the action figure mistakes a claw machine for a rocket and climbs in, pursued by the sheriff.

The boy's sadistic next-door neighbor grabs the sheriff and the action figure with the claw and takes them to his house, where they encounter his mutant toys, made from parts of toys the neighbor has destroyed.
After evading the neighbor's dog, the action figure sees a television commercial promoting toys identical to himself and suffers an existential crisis, finally realizing that he is a toy.
He attempts to fly, but falls and breaks his arm off.
After the neighbor's toys repair the action figure, the neighbor tapes him to a firework rocket, planning to blow him up the following day.
Overnight, the sheriff helps the action figure realize that his purpose is to make the boy happy, reinvigorating him.

The next morning, as the neighbor prepares to launch the rocket, the sheriff rallies the mutant toys to help him, and together, they come to life and frighten the neighbor, telling him to play nice with his toys from now on.
After the neighbor flees, the sheriff and the action figure pursue the family's moving truck, but the dog, who had been locked out of the house, attacks the sheriff.
The action figure jumps off the truck and fights the dog off, while the sheriff climbs up and pushes a remote-control car out to rescue the action figure.
The other toys think the sheriff is harming the remote-control car and promptly throw him out of the truck.
The sheriff and the action figure race after the truck on the remote-control car, but his batteries run out.
The sheriff ignites the rocket strapped to the action figure, and the action figure opens his wings to sever the tape just before the rocket explodes.
The sheriff and the action figure glide through the sunroof of the family's car, landing safely inside.
On Christmas in the new house, the toys happily listen to the boy opening his presents, no longer concerned over new toys replacing them.
When the boy receives a puppy however, the sheriff and the action figure nervously smile at each other.
The father and the mother, a clownfish couple who are waiting for their eggs to hatch, live on the edge of a reef.
After a barracuda knocks the father unconscious, the father awakens to find the mother and all but one of the eggs gone.
The father names the surviving child and vows to keep him safe.
Years later, the father and the son live in a secluded sea anemone.
The son is eager to start school and explore the outside world; however the father remains anxious and hyperprotective of his son.
While dropping the son off at school, the father warns the teacher of the son's deformed pelvic fin.
After discovering the son's class will be visiting the "drop-off", where the reef meets the open sea, the father panics and tries to withdraw the son from school.
The son defiantly swims to a nearby speedboat to prove his independence and is captured by a pair of scuba divers.
The father frantically races after the boat, disappearing into the horizon.
He meets a blue tang with short-term memory loss who offers to help him locate his son.
The pair encounter a great white shark who is part of a support group of sharks trying to abstain from eating fish.
At the meeting, the father finds a diver's mask from the boat with an address written on it.
When the father accidentally injures the blue tang, the shark smells her blood and relapses into a rampage that sets off old naval mines.
As they escape, the blue tang recalls that she can read the address.
Meanwhile, the son is placed in a fish tank in a dentist's office in the city.
He meets the tank's gang, led by a scarred Moorish idol and consisting of a sea star, a striped damselfish, a royal gramma, a pufferfish, a yellow tang, and a cleaner shrimp.
They inform him that the dentist plans to gift the son to his hyperactive niece, who has an infamous history of killing her pet fish.
To prevent this, the leader hatches an escape plan: the son, the smallest of the gang, will clog the tank's filter, forcing the dentist to clean it and bag the fish.
Then, they can roll their bags out of the window and into the harbour.
The son attempts the plan but is nearly killed by the filter's machinery in the process, causing the leader to feel deeply regretful.
The blue tang accidentally drops the mask into an abyss and encourages the father to help her search for it.
They find the mask but are attacked by an anglerfish.
The blue tang exploits the anglerfish's light to read the address while the father traps the anglerfish with the mask.
Their victory boosts the father's confidence and helps the blue tang remember the address.
The father tries to continue his search without the blue tang until she convinces a school of moonfish to give them directions to an ocean current.
On their way, the father and the blue tang become trapped in a forest of jellyfish.
While trying to escape, they are both stung and fall unconscious.
The father and the blue tang awaken in the ocean current with a large group of sea turtles, including a turtle and his son.
The turtle teaches the father to relax and be less worried about the son.
News of the father's journey spreads across the ocean and reaches a pelican who regularly converses with the tank's gang.
The pelican informs the son of the father's efforts; inspired, the son successfully clogs the filter and the tank quickly becomes covered in green algae.
However, this plan is foiled due to the dentist cleaning the tank while the fish sleep and installing a newer filtration system.
After leaving the current, the father and the blue tang become lost and are consumed by a blue whale.
The father fears the worst, but the blue tang urges him to trust the whale, which safely expels them through its blowhole into the city's harbour.
The pelican rescues the father and the blue tang from a flock of seagulls and delivers them to the dentist's office, where they see the son playing dead to fake out the niece.
The dentist forces the pelican out and the leader helps the son escape down the sink drain and into the harbour.
Believing the son is genuinely dead, the father says goodbye to the blue tang and leaves, but the blue tang soon finds the son and reunites them.
A fishing trawler captures the blue tang and a school of groupers.
The son persuades the father to let him swim into the net and lead the groupers down; the fish in turn break the trawler, freeing the blue tang.
The father praises the son's bravery and tells him about his own journey.
In the mid-1940s, a man is a war veteran and the youngest son of a don.
The don is head of a mafia family and runs it with his eldest son,
and his adopted son, a lawyer who is the family's consigliere.
At his sister's wedding to her groom, the youngest son introduces his family to his girlfriend.
The youngest son tells his girlfriend stories of his family but makes it clear that he wants no part in his family's business.
The don fulfils his homeland's tradition of granting favors on his daughter's wedding day to a succession of hopeful visitors.
One is his godson, a singer and actor, who cannot get an upcoming film role because a studio owner and producer has a grudge against the singer.
The don sends the consigliere to another city to persuade the producer to relent but the producer will not budge.
The consigliere departs and the next morning, the producer wakes to find the severed head of his prized $600,000 racehorse in his bed with him.
A terrified producer relents and the singer gets the role.
Approaching Christmas, the youngest son becomes embroiled in family affairs when the don is gunned down by two assailants.
The don had earlier refused to offer protection to a drug baron for dealing narcotics in the city.
The drug baron has the support of a rival family, who garrote the don's notorious enforcer when he attempts to become a mole in the drug baron's operation.
While the don survives the attempt and recovers at the hospital, the hot-tempered eldest son takes over the family as acting boss.
He has the youngest son live at the house for his protection, as his successful revenge hit on the rival boss's son has led to war between the two gangs.
The youngest son visits his father in hospital to be told that a police captain has had the don's bodyguards ejected from the hospital, clearing the way for a second attempt on the don's life.
The youngest son visits his father and, realizing his jeopardy, moves him to another hospital room then stands guard outside the hospital.
He scares the drug baron's assassins off but an angry captain returns and breaks the youngest son's jaw for defying him.
Soon after, the consigliere arrives with more bodyguards and the captain backs down to the lawyer's demands.

Being an outsider to the family business and seen as harmless, the youngest son later proposes a meeting between himself, the drug baron and the captain at which he'll kill them both to keep his father safe.
Initially amused, the family approve his plan and have a gun planted at the meeting place: a restaurant.
At the meeting, the youngest son shoots both men dead then flees the country.
He takes refuge in his family's native land to escape the police and the ire of the other gangs until the heat dies down.
He falls in love with a local woman and marries her.
Back in the city, war has broken out between the five families.
The eldest son discovers that the sister was being abused by her husband.
At first, the eldest son pummels her husband in public and warns him never to touch the sister again.
However, after a fierce beating from her husband, the sister appeals to her family.
A furious eldest son sets off for her house but is ambushed and murdered at a highway toll booth.
The recovering don is told of the eldest son's death and orders an end to hostilities with no vengeance.

He calls a meeting with the heads of the other families in the city and negotiates peace between them all, conceding to a controlled drug trade in return for an end to all vendettas and for the youngest son's safe return home.
Meanwhile, the youngest son survives a hit in his family's native land, which instead kills his wife via car bombing.
He returns home, slowly taking over the family business from his father.
He marries his girlfriend and promises to legitimize the family's operations within five years.
The youngest son visits another city to negotiate a deal with a Jewish mobster and casino mogul, under whose protection a relative has been living.
The youngest son offers to buy out the mogul's stake in the family casinos, but the mogul refuses and flaunts his support from another boss.
After the mogul leaves, the youngest son reprimands the relative for defending the mogul and warns him never to side against the family ever again.
After the peace meeting, the don realizes that the other boss is the mastermind behind the eldest son's death, not the rival boss.

He predicts to the youngest son that a traitor within the family will reveal himself by offering to broker a meeting between the youngest son and the other boss's family but will use it to have the youngest son assassinated.
The don dies of a heart attack while playing with his grandson, the youngest son's son.
